messages.content: Analyze this sentence.  "Consydre thou myne condicyon; reflecte upon myne fader. Shall I forsake hym, when he is strycken wyth blyndnesse and destytute, to wrastle wyth infirmitie and penurye, when it lyeth wythin my poure to rendre hys latter yeeres fylled wyth comforte and joye?" Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.

message.content:
The sentence employs archaic Middle English spelling and syntax to evoke a tone of solemn moral duty.
duty

The speaker addresses the listener directly, urging them to consider the father's dire physical and financial state as a reason for care.
care

This rhetorical structure highlights the contrast between the potential suffering of the elderly parent and the son's ability to provide comfort.
comfort
